newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA LOSE THEIR HEADS IN DEFEAT BY BOLIVIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA LOSE THEIR HEADS IN DEFEAT BY BOLIVIA.

text.p: Argentina had two players sent off and became involved in a brawl that held up play for nearly ten minutes as they lost 2-1 to Bolivia in a World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.
Dozens of police came onto the field near the end of the game to stop fighting after the Argentine players lost their heads. The Bolivian players left the field until order was restored.
The trouble appeared to start with a row between Argentina striker Julio Cruz and members of the Bolivian team bench.
During the brawl, one Argentine player spat in the direction of Bolivian fans while others, visibly wild with rage, lashed out a officials.
After the interruption, the final two mintues were played out with further incident to allow Bolivia to claim a deserved win.
Fernando Ochoaizpur scored the winner for Bolivia early in the second half, hammering in a rebound after Argentina goalkeeper Ignacio Gonzalez had parried three shots in succession.
Earlier, Marco Sandy had given Bolivia an early lead before Nestor Gorosito equalised from a penalty in the 42nd minute.
The result enabled Bolivia to pull level on points with Argentina, who began the day third in the nine-team South American group.

Bolivia's problem now is they have only one of their remaining seven games at home. Despite Argentina's complaining about the altitude, Paraguay, Peru, Chile and Colombia have all earned draws in La Paz.
The atmosphere in the run up to the game had been tense.

Argentina had complained bitterly about playing in La Paz, 3,600 metres above sea level, and coach Daniel Passarella had inflamed Bolivian passions with a comment that it was "inhuman" to play soccer there.
Tensions increased further on Tuesday when Passarella stormed out of a press conference after a local reporter accused him of being "cowardly."
Argentina, who have dropped points at home to Paraguay and Chile and lost away to Ecuador, were their own worst enemies as the argued with their opponents, the match officials and amongst themselves.
In sulky mood, they still appeared to be feeling sorry for themselves at the start of the game, and their defence was in complete disarry early on.

Bolivia had already created two excellent chances, the first of which was wasted by Limbert Guttierez who fell over the ball when he had a clear run on goal, before Sandy struck in the eighth minute with far post header.
Argentine defender Hernan Diaz wasted precious minutes in a futile argument with officials on the touchline because the referee would not let him stay on the field with a bleeding nose.

Diaz missed nearly ten minutes of first half action and when he had to leave the field again shortly afterwards, members of the Argentine bench began arguing with officials and police on the touchline.
Bolivia concentrated on playing and could have increased their lead.

But Argentina, in their first decent attack, equalised in the 42nd minute. Striker Julio Cruz was needlessly brought down by Ivan Castillo and Gorosito's penalty sent Bolivia goalkeeper Carlos Trucco the wrong way.
Argentina were behind again early in the second half after their defence allowed Bolivia to take pot-shots at Gonzalez, who defended three efforts but was powerless to stop Ochaoizpur's drive.

Argentine coach Daniel Passarella immediately brought on his trump card, midfielder Ariel Ortega, who hit the underside of the crossbar shortly afterwards in his team's only decent second half effort.
The Argentines, already on edge, lost control of themselves after Ochoaizpur's goal early in the second half.
Defender Nelson Vivas was sent off in the 65th minute for a vicious foul committed only minutes after he had been booked.

Gustavo Zapata, booked in the first half, committed an ugly foul in the second and was also dismissed. Instead of leaving the field immediately, he walked over and began arguing with the player who suffered the foul.
Teams:

Bolivia - 1-Carlos Trucco, 19-Ivan Castillo, 3-Marco Antonio Sandy, 5-Oscar Sanchez, 4-Miguel Rimba, 7-Sergio Castillo, 2- Fernando Ochoaizpur, 6-Vladimir Soria, 20-Ramiro Castillo, 9- Jaime Moreno (17-Demetrio Angola, 70), 10-Limbert Gutirrez.

Argentina: 1-Ignacio Gonzlez, 8-Hernan Diaz, 2-Roberto Sensini, 4-Nelson Vivas, 6-Pablo Paz, 5-Gustavo Zapata, 3-Juan Pablo Sorin, 16-Diego Cagna (10-Ariel Ortega, 52), 19-Nestor Gorosito (11-Juan Beron, 46), 7-Marcelo Delgado (18-Jose Calderon), 9-Julio Cruz.
